name: Mangal Pandey
role: Sepoy who sparked the Barrackpore uprising
contribution: On 29 March 1857 at Barrackpore, sepoy Mangal Pandey attacked British officers, an act remembered as an early flashpoint of the uprising.
context: North and central India during the anti-colonial uprising of 1857-1859.
impact: His action became an important symbol in later accounts of the 1857 rebellion, while the wider uprising developed through many separate regional causes and actors.
highlight: Mangal Pandey's 29 March 1857 action at Barrackpore became one of the best-known early flashpoints of the rebellion.
seoTitle: Mangal Pandey: Barrackpore and the 1857 Rebellion
seoDescription: Learn how Mangal Pandey's action at Barrackpore on 29 March 1857 entered the history and memory of the Indian Rebellion.
shortAnswer: Mangal Pandey was a sepoy whose 29 March 1857 action at Barrackpore became an early flashpoint of the Indian Rebellion.
